learning_outcomes.text: The student must demonstrate an adequate knowledge of chemical and electrochemical phenomena of broad engineering interest.
The student must demonstrate knowledge and thus analyze the essential parameters that control the chemical phenomena that are the basis of industrial technologies.

syllabus_topics: Origins of quantum mechanics: classical radiation theory and photon theory.
Interactions between matter and radiant energy.
Electronic structure of the atom and chemical bonding according to quantum mechanics.
Chemical bonding: valence bond and molecular orbital theories.
Genesis of valence and conduction bands in conductors and semiconductors, intrinsic and doped; band structure and photovoltaic effect.
Defects present in crystals (point, line, and plane defects) and their influence on electrical and mechanical properties.
Nuclear chemistry and radioactivity and applications.
Elements of flame chemistry, flammability limits, autoignition curves.
Electrolysis and electrodeposition methods: electroplating and electroforming.
Measurement of equilibrium constants with electrochemical methods.
Iron, aluminum, copper and their alloys.
Technologies for energy production and storage.
Organic chemistry: hydrocarbons, functional groups, reaction classes.

Stoichiometry and thermochemistry of combustion reactions: higher and lower heating value, theoretical combustion air, theoretical combustion temperature, chimney losses, thermal potential, smoke analysis.
assessment_rules: The final grade is formulated by the Examination Committee based on the adequacy of the student's answers to the questions posed. The final grade is also appropriately justified to the student.
bibliography: Oxtoby, Gillis, Campion, Chimica Moderna Edises.
